title: Osmoregulation & ADH
examples: What happens to my urine if I drink too much water?
How does ADH help my body keep the right water level?
Can you explain the role of the pituitary gland here?

explain.say: Our bodies must keep a careful balance of water.
This balance is called osmoregulation, keeping salt and water levels stable.
When we are dehydrated, blood becomes saltier, triggering a response.
The pituitary gland releases antidiuretic hormone, or ADH, in response.
ADH tells the kidneys to reabsorb more water back into the blood.
In everyday life, drinking too much salty food can cause this process to kick in.

faq.a: Osmoregulation is the process where organisms maintain the correct water and salt balance in their bodies. It keeps the concentration of substances stable.
asks: How does the body control water levels?
What is the balance of water in the body?

faq.a: ADH stands for antidiuretic hormone. It is a hormone that controls how much water the kidneys keep.
asks: What is the name of the water-retaining hormone?

faq.q: What happens if I drink a lot of water quickly?
faq.a: If you drink too much water, your blood becomes less concentrated, and ADH levels will drop. This means you will pass out a lot of very dilute urine.
asks: Will I pee a lot if I drink too much?
What if my blood gets too watery?

faq.a: ADH is released by the pituitary gland into the bloodstream. It then travels to the kidneys to do its job.

faq.q: Why does dehydration make my urine dark?
faq.a: When you are dehydrated, your blood is saltier, so your kidneys hold onto every bit of water. This makes the waste product, urine, more concentrated and darker.

facts: Osmoregulation maintains the internal balance of water and salts.
ADH is released by the pituitary gland when the body is dehydrated.
High ADH levels cause the kidneys to reabsorb more water.
When water is scarce, urine becomes more concentrated.

quiz.say: If a person has been sweating heavily and is dehydrated, what will the pituitary gland likely release more of?
quiz.why: Dehydration means the blood is saltier, which triggers the pituitary to release more ADH to save water.

wrong.0: Insulin controls blood sugar, which is a different system entirely.
wrong.1: The body has a specific hormone for water balance in this situation.
wrong.3: Aldosterone mainly controls salt levels, not directly the water retention signaled by ADH.

quiz.say: If the kidneys are working correctly when you are dehydrated, what will the urine be?
quiz.why: The purpose of ADH is to make the kidneys save water, resulting in highly concentrated urine.

wrong.0: Clear urine suggests normal hydration, not the state of dehydration.
wrong.1: Pink urine usually indicates the presence of blood, which is a different issue.
wrong.3: Dilute urine means too much water was lost, which happens when ADH is low.

quiz.say: If the body has too much water, what happens to ADH levels?
quiz.why: When the blood is too watery, the body signals the pituitary to reduce ADH release, allowing more water to be excreted.

wrong.0: High ADH would cause the body to hold onto water, making the problem worse.
wrong.1: ADH is not completely stopped; it just decreases significantly.
wrong.2: The levels must change to correct the water imbalance.
